elements.texte:
[cheerful] The marketing team wants to remind each customer to reorder, at the right time.

That time depends on the average gap between two of the customer’s orders.

To calculate it, we get the order dates from the orders table.

And a customer who ordered only once will get their reminder after 10 days.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] In the table, each order has its own row, all customers together.

Customer 2, Lucas Bernard, ordered on July 5, then on July 20.

To measure his gap, the second order has to read a date on another row.

And this date must be the one of the same customer’s previous order.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] With lag of order underscore date, each row reads the date of the previous row.

Partition by separates the customers, and order by sorts each one’s orders by date.

For each customer’s first order, lag returns null, since no order comes before it.

Lead reads the next row: then it’s the last order that shows null.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] For the gap, julian day converts each date into a number of days.

The difference gives the gap: Lucas Bernard reordered after 15 days.

Sophie Martin placed two orders on July 2: the gap between them is 0 days.

Her next order, on July 28, comes 26 days after the previous one.

With no previous order, no gap: the first orders stay at null.

[cheerful] Without partition by, the orders, sorted by customer then by date, form a single sequence.

Lucas Bernard’s very first order then reads Sophie Martin’s last one.

The calculated gap is minus 23 days: a result that makes no sense.

With partition by customer underscore ID, each customer keeps their own sequence.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] First, a WITH named gaps calculates each order’s gap.

Then, A-V-G calculates each customer’s average.

For Sophie Martin, the gaps between two successive orders are 0 and 26 days.

So the average gap is 0 plus 26, divided by 2, equals 13 days.

The null of her first order is ignored by A-V-G.

Hugo Laurent and Gabriel Michel placed only one order each:

No way to calculate a gap between two orders.

Coalesce so replaces their null average with 10 days, the chosen default value.

Each customer will get their reminder at the right time: 8 reminders are scheduled.
